name: Blueprint Biosecurity (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: a pandemic kills people everywhere and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population.
summary: Blueprint Biosecurity (Washington, DC) works on defences against any airborne pandemic: far-UVC light, glycol vapours and other ways to clean indoor air, and pandemic-grade reusable respirators, through research syntheses ('Blueprints') and research grants to universities. This model of all its work in 2024 (its latest Form 990, $3.10M) comes to about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000, from {{low}} to {{high}} on its plausible range: each dollar is valued as a typical pandemic project's cut in the forecast risk (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model, the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament's experts), weighted by how far each programme's outputs were taken up, deaths valued like every death (a COVID-scale pandemic's at COVID's age mix) and the future lost counted only where you count lives that never start (0% by default). The biggest uncertainties are the discount rate, the years a cut counts and how much a typical dollar cuts the risk (Rethink calls its figures placeholders; the range runs ten times either way); the next dollar counts at {{row:marginal_vs_past_average}} of the past average because its main funder has since raised its support several-fold. Every branch is discounted for missing data: no outcome of the work on the risk is measured.

sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

story.sentence: $1,000 funds defences against airborne pandemics, such as far-UVC light and better respirators. Every **{1000 / (1000 * deaths_averted * total_adj * marginal_vs_past_average / cost_total)|$}** saves **a life** on average.

rows.formula: -((cost_total * ai_cost_share / 1e6 * ai_future_per_million * ai_discounted_years) + (cost_total * bio_cost_share / 1e6 * bio_future_per_million * bio_discounted_years) + (cost_total * nuclear_cost_share / 1e6 * nuclear_future_per_million * nuclear_discounted_years) + (pol_wins * pol_p_success * pol_relative_cut * pol_future_per_year * pol_discounted_years) + (fb_work_dollars / 1e6 * fb_credit_share * fb_future_per_million * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, years_of_impact))) * $lives_added * $animal_dalys_per_person_year_world
rows.explainer: A future kept is also every animal raised to feed it: each future person-year at the suffering of the animals an average person eats in a year today (docs/normalization.md 2.25). Suffering always counts, whatever lives that never start count; the farmed animals' own good days count where you set them to. Held at today's diet: no forecast of what people will eat is used.

rows.explainer: How far a typical pandemic project's cut per dollar applies to the far-UVC work: it commissions the studies that stand between far-UVC and deployment (eye tolerance, indoor air chemistry, airborne inactivation, transmission models) and wrote the Blueprint for Far-UVC (published 2025), which its 2025 annual report calls field-defining; but no deployment, guidance or standard has yet followed, and the main real-world efficacy studies (EXHALE, DEMIST, a tuberculosis transmission study) report in 2026. Research a step before uptake: 0.8, our judgment, a little above the template's 0.7 for typical research because the studies target the stated barriers; 0.4 to 1.2.

rows.label: Biosecurity and government affairs: uptake against a typical pandemic project
rows.explainer: Stakeholder education, strategy and partnerships around the programmes in 2024, including early advocacy for advanced respirators for critical workers ($3,044 of direct lobbying, Schedule C), before its government affairs team began (2025): no output of its own in 2024 to judge, so the template's 0.7 for typical work, 0.3 to 1.1.

rows.label: Glycol vapours and other air cleaning: uptake against a typical pandemic project
rows.explainer: Desk research on an underexplored technology: glycol vapours were studied in the 1940s and have open questions on safety and effect in occupied rooms (annual report, p. 7). The 2024 work led to a funded research programme (seven grants in 2026), but whether any of it ends in deployment is further off than for far-UVC or respirators: 0.6, our judgment, below the template's 0.7, 0.3 to 1.1.

rows.label: Protective equipment: uptake against a typical pandemic project
rows.explainer: The Next-Gen PPE Blueprint (June 2024) and Towards a Theory of Pandemic-Proof PPE (May 2024) make a costed case for stockpiling reusable respirators; their figures went into a Federation of American Scientists policy memo on caches of reusable respirators (October 2024), but its author, Aman Patel, is Blueprint's own PPE lead, so that is Blueprint's output, not uptake by others; the six mentions of reusable respirators in the FY2026 appropriations bills came from its 2025 government affairs work, outside this model's year. No uptake by others is shown for 2024: 0.8, our judgment, as the far-UVC work (uvc_evidence_adj), near the template's 0.7 for typical research, 0.4 to 1.2.

rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the pandemics counted: the technologies Blueprint works on are also everyday infection control. Far-UVC and upper-room germicidal light are used against tuberculosis in clinics and shelters, cleaner indoor air cuts seasonal influenza and COVID-19 transmission, and stockpiled reusable respirators also protect workers in wildfire smoke and ordinary outbreaks. Its research makes such use likelier and safer, less a small harm: far-UVC can add ozone and secondary particles indoors if deployed before that research settles it (the work it funds at MIT, Penn State and Colorado State). Net 15% of the modelled value, our judgment, 2% to 50%: these are tools with use between pandemics, not only in one.

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire (in the shared cut): nothing in Blueprint's work advances dangerous biology; it studies defences (light, vapours, respirators) against any airborne pathogen. 0, down to -2% for the small chance its testing of how pathogens are inactivated helps someone, our judgment.

rows.label: Harm: information hazards and attention, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire: Blueprint publishes no threat analyses; its reports describe defences and the gaps in stockpiles, which a bad actor learns little from. 0, down to -2%, our judgment.
